title: Saudi Arabia Launches New One-Year Multiple-Entry Umrah Visa With 90-Day Stay
excerpt: The Kingdom's Hajj Ministry introduces a dedicated Umrah visa valid for one year with multiple entries and up to 90 days per visit, expanding access for pilgrims from India and other major Muslim-majority nations.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Saudi Arabia's new Umrah visa allows multiple entries and 90-day stays for one year.
  • Pilgrims from India, UK, Malaysia, Turkey, Egypt, Iraq, and UAE can apply for the new visa.
  • The visa simplifies travel for Indian pilgrims, eliminating the need for repeated applications.
  • This initiative supports Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 to boost religious tourism significantly.
  • Saudi Arabia aims to increase annual Umrah visitors from 10 million to 30 million.

Target Annual Umrah Visitors by 2030
Saudi Ministry of Hajj and Umrah
  • Saudi Arabia's Hajj Ministry has launched a new dedicated one-year, multiple-entry Umrah visa allowing stays of up to 90 days per visit
  • The visa is available to pilgrims from countries including India, the UK, Malaysia, Turkey, Egypt, Iraq, and the UAE
  • India sends one of the largest contingents of Umrah pilgrims annually; the new visa eliminates the need for repeated single-entry applications
  • The move is part of Saudi Arabia's broader Vision 2030 strategy to expand religious tourism beyond the annual Hajj season

Saudi Arabia has introduced a new dedicated Umrah visa valid for one year with multiple entries, allowing pilgrims to stay up to 90 days per visit. The announcement by the Kingdom's Ministry of Hajj and Umrah marks a significant expansion of access for Muslim travelers, particularly from India, which sends one of the world's largest contingents of Umrah pilgrims annually.

The new visa covers pilgrims from a broad list of countries, including India, the United Kingdom, Malaysia, Turkey, Egypt, Iraq, and the UAE. It is distinct from Saudi Arabia's existing tourist e-visa, which also permits Umrah but is designed primarily for leisure travel.

What Changes for Indian Pilgrims

Previously, most Indian pilgrims seeking to perform Umrah relied on single-entry visas valid for 90 days, which required a fresh application for each trip. The new multiple-entry format allows families and frequent worshippers to visit Makkah and Madinah multiple times within a year without restarting the visa process.

For the Indian Muslim diaspora in the US, UK, and Gulf countries, the development simplifies logistics considerably. NRIs holding valid visas can plan multiple visits around work schedules, school holidays, and Ramadan without the bureaucratic overhead of separate applications each time.

Part of a Broader Strategy

The new Umrah visa aligns with Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 goals, which include increasing annual Umrah visitors from approximately 10 million to 30 million. The Kingdom has invested heavily in expanding the capacity of the Grand Mosque in Makkah and improving transportation infrastructure between the holy cities.

Saudi Arabia has also introduced a new catering policy for Umrah pilgrims from select countries and recently overhauled its Nusuk digital platform to streamline visa applications, hotel bookings, and ground transport arrangements.

Impact on Indian Pilgrims
›Eliminates need for repeated single-entry applications.
›Facilitates multiple visits for families and frequent worshippers.
›Simplifies logistics for NRIs in the US, UK, and Gulf countries.
›Aligns with broader goals of enhancing religious tourism.

Visa Details

The new one-year Umrah visa requires applicants to have a passport valid for at least six months, confirmed accommodation through the Nusuk platform, and a mandatory meningococcal ACWY vaccination certificate. Fees are expected to be in line with the existing e-visa pricing — approximately SAR 300 to 480 (roughly $80 to $130) depending on processing speed and insurance bundling.

Applications can be submitted through the official Nusuk Umrah portal or authorized travel agents licensed by the Ministry of Hajj and Umrah.

Vision 2030 Goals
›Increase Umrah visitors from 10 million to 30 million.
›Expand Grand Mosque capacity and improve transport infrastructure.
›Streamline visa applications through the Nusuk platform.
›Position Saudi Arabia as a year-round religious travel destination.

What's Next

The announcement comes as Saudi Arabia prepares for the upcoming Hajj season, with the Kingdom also expanding its 96-hour transit visa program that allows Umrah during layovers for passengers flying Saudi Arabian Airlines or flynas. Together, these measures are designed to position Saudi Arabia as a year-round religious travel destination rather than one defined solely by the annual Hajj pilgrimage.
